definition: Implicate means to show or suggest, through evidence, that someone was involved in a crime or wrongdoing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word implicate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know implicate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Grainy security footage seemed to implicate the night-shift supervisor in the warehouse break-in, though he insisted he had only been checking a tripped alarm.
To associate someone with a scandal merely links their name to it loosely; to implicate them means real evidence points to their actual involvement.
To implicate someone suggests involvement in wrongdoing; to incriminate them means the evidence points squarely at their guilt.

To compromise someone is to damage their standing or leave them exposed to suspicion — leaked emails can compromise an official without showing any wrongdoing at all. To implicate someone, the evidence must point to their actual involvement in the deed itself, not merely dent their reputation.

To entangle someone is to catch them in something messy and hard to escape — paperwork, a lawsuit, a feud — with no claim about guilt at all. To implicate them is sharper: evidence suggests they took part in the wrongdoing itself.

To embroil someone is to drag them into a conflict or scandal, where the emphasis is the turmoil around them. To implicate them is quieter and more pointed: a document or a fingerprint suggests their own involvement in the wrong, whether or not any public storm follows.
to officially clear someone of blame
to show that someone is not guilty

Implicate means to show or suggest, through evidence, that someone was involved in a crime or wrongdoing.
The forensic accountant's report appeared to implicate the nonprofit's treasurer in the disappearance of nearly forty thousand dollars in donations.
The report's financial evidence connects the treasurer to the missing money — it suggests her involvement without formally charging her with anything, which is exactly what implicate means.
Formal / legal & journalistic
Implicate appears constantly in reporting on investigations: documents, footage, or testimony implicates a person — it suggests their involvement.
Keep it distinct from indict (also taught in this unit), which is the formal legal act of charging someone with a crime: evidence can implicate a person for years without them ever being indicted.

For two weeks the audit of the charity's books pointed nowhere in particular.
Then an examiner noticed that the same login had approved each of the eleven suspicious transfers, always minutes after midnight.
The login belonged to the deputy director.
It was the first find that could implicate him, rather than merely embarrass the organization.

The login record was different: it tied one person's hands to the transfers themselves, and the board finally called the police.
